question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.
With the harsh words of the boss, Srujan felt sad, but his colleague's words created insult to injury.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. added insult to injury.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to add insult to injury" means to make a bad situation even worse by doing or saying something further hurtful, especially after someone has already been wronged or hurt. (जले पर नमक छिड़कना)
◦ Example: He forgot my birthday, and to add insult to injury, he later criticised the cake I baked myself.

• In the given sentence, Srujan already felt sad because of the boss's harsh words; his colleague's words made the situation worse — hence "added insult to injury" fits perfectly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "attached insult to injury" is incorrect because "attached" is not part of this fixed idiomatic expression; the correct verb used is "added".

• Option 2: "provoked insult to injury" is incorrect for the same reason — "provoked" does not fit the fixed idiom, which always uses "added".

• Option 3: "added injury to insult" reverses the correct word order of the idiom; the standard, fixed form is "add insult to injury", not "injury to insult".

NOTE

• Idioms are fixed expressions — even a small change in word order or a substituted word (as in Options 1, 2 and 3) makes the expression incorrect, even if the individual words are related in meaning.

• Other common idioms of "making things worse" tested by SSC: "the last straw" (the final problem in a series that makes a situation unbearable) and "to rub salt into the wound" (to make someone's pain or embarrassment worse).

question:
Select the option that correctly expresses the following sentence in passive voice.
The child will recite the poem.
option_1: By child poem will be recited.
option_2: The poem will be recited by the child.
option_3: The poem is recited by the child.
option_4: The poem will recite by the child.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The poem will be recited by the child.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "The child will recite the poem" is an assertive sentence in the Simple Future Tense.

• Rule — Simple Future Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + will/shall + V1 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + will/shall + be + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "the poem" becomes the subject; the auxiliary "will" is retained and followed by "be"; the verb "recite" becomes its past participle "recited"; and "the child" becomes the agent introduced by "by".
◦ Passive: The poem will be recited by the child.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because it drops the required auxiliary "will be" and wrongly begins with "By child", producing an ungrammatical sentence with the wrong word order.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "is recited" is the passive form of the Simple Present Tense, not the Simple Future Tense used in the given sentence.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "will recite" keeps the verb in its active form; a passive sentence must use "be + V3" (i.e., "will be recited"), not the bare active verb.

NOTE

• In the passive voice, the modal auxiliary (will/shall/can/may/must, etc.) is always retained exactly as in the active sentence, and is followed by "be + V3".

• Intransitive verbs (verbs without an object, e.g. "sleep", "arrive") cannot be converted into the passive voice, since there is no object to become the subject.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
You need to acknowledge the itinary and accommodation details of your journey as per the given calendar.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. itinary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "itinary" is a misspelling. The correct spelling is "itinerary" — a planned route or schedule of a journey, listing the places to be visited.

• Spelling key: I-TIN-ER-ARY. Note the extra syllable "er" between "itin" and "ary", which is often dropped by mistake, giving the incorrect form "itinary".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "calendar" is spelt correctly and fits the sentence, so it does not contain an error.

• Option 2: "accommodation" is spelt correctly — note the double "c" and double "m" — so it does not contain an error.

• Option 3: "acknowledge" is spelt correctly and used appropriately as the main verb of the sentence, so it does not contain an error.

NOTE

• Other commonly misspelt travel-related words asked by SSC: "itinerary", "accommodation", "boulevard", "embarkation" and "reservation".

• Always check words with silent or easily-dropped internal syllables — words like "temperature", "library" and "February" are misspelt in the same way, by dropping an internal syllable.

question:
Choose the correct meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence.
When I was in Class 5, I won the first prize in extempore at my school.
option_1: A short piece of writing on a subject
option_3: A speech delivered without prior preparation or rehearsal
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. A speech delivered without prior preparation or rehearsal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "extempore" means a speech or performance given without any prior preparation, notes, or rehearsal, spoken spontaneously on the spot. (बिना पूर्व तैयारी के दिया गया भाषण)
◦ Example: The chief guest was asked to speak extempore since the scheduled speaker had not arrived.

• It comes from the Latin phrase "ex tempore", literally meaning "out of the time" i.e., something done on the spur of the moment.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "A short piece of writing on a subject" describes an essay, not "extempore", which is a spoken, unrehearsed activity.

• Option 2: "A sports event" is incorrect; "extempore" has nothing to do with sport — it is purely a speaking activity.

• Option 4: "A dramatic performance on stage" describes a play/drama, which (unlike extempore) is scripted and rehearsed in advance.

NOTE

• Related word: "impromptu" is a close synonym of "extempore", also meaning done without preparation.

• Contrast with "rehearsed", "scripted" and "prepared speech", which are antonymous concepts frequently used as distractors in such questions.

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
A. fell before me
B. a carcass of an animal
C. when suddenly
D. my heart skipped a beat
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. DCBA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A meaningful sentence needs a clear main clause followed by a subordinate clause introduced by a time-conjunction like "when".

• Part D ("my heart skipped a beat") is the natural starting main clause — it states the main event/reaction.

• Part C ("when suddenly") must follow D, introducing the cause of the reaction with the time-conjunction "when".

• Part B ("a carcass of an animal") is the subject of the subordinate clause, and Part A ("fell before me") is its verb phrase, so B must be followed by A to complete the clause.

• Combining in the order D-C-B-A gives: "My heart skipped a beat when suddenly a carcass of an animal fell before me." — a grammatically complete and meaningful sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (BACD) is incorrect because it begins with "a carcass of an animal fell before me my heart skipped a beat when suddenly", which is disjointed and does not form a coherent sentence.

• Option 2 (CDBA) is incorrect because it begins with "when suddenly", leaving the subordinate clause without a preceding main clause, which is grammatically incomplete on its own.

• Option 3 (ABCD) is incorrect because it produces "fell before me a carcass of an animal when suddenly my heart skipped a beat", which reverses the logical cause-and-effect order of the sentence.

NOTE

• In sentence-rearrangement questions, look for the part that can stand as an independent main clause — it usually comes first, especially when another part starts with a subordinating conjunction like "when", "because", or "although".

• Time-conjunctions such as "when", "as", "while" typically introduce the clause describing the surprising or sudden event, which logically follows the main clause describing the reaction.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A) So then why are not Silicon Valley entrepreneurs clamouring to decode the ancient wisdom?
B) The failure rate in finding a new drug is as high as 95%.
C) Because these once-thriving cultures are now reduced to an endangered tribe.
D) According to industry data, it takes $2.6 billion and, on average, fourteen years to develop a new drug.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. DBAC.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A coherent paragraph must move logically from fact → consequence → question → explanation.

• Part D opens the paragraph with a factual statistic: "it takes $2.6 billion and, on average, fourteen years to develop a new drug" — a natural starting point.

• Part B logically follows D, adding a related statistic: "the failure rate in finding a new drug is as high as 95%", reinforcing how costly and difficult drug development is.

• Part A then raises a question prompted by B: given this huge cost and failure rate, "why are not Silicon Valley entrepreneurs clamouring to decode the ancient wisdom?" — implying that ancient/traditional knowledge could be a cheaper alternative source of remedies.

• Part C closes the paragraph by answering/explaining A: "because these once-thriving cultures are now reduced to an endangered tribe" — i.e., that ancient wisdom is being lost, which is precisely the problem.

• The order D-B-A-C therefore produces a logically complete paragraph.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (BADC) is incorrect because it opens with the failure-rate statistic (B) before establishing the context of drug development cost (D), disturbing the logical fact-then-consequence flow.

• Option 2 (DCBA) is incorrect because it places C (about endangered cultures) immediately after D, before the connecting statistic in B and the question in A have been introduced, breaking the cause-effect chain.

• Option 4 (ACDB) is incorrect because it opens with the question in A before any supporting statistics (D, B) have been given, so the question has no context to refer back to.

NOTE

• In paragraph (para-jumble) questions, identify the sentence that best serves as an opening statement (usually a general fact, free of pronouns referring backward) and the sentence that best serves as a concluding/explanatory statement (often containing "because", "so", or a resolving idea).

• Look out for logical connectors like "so then why" and "because", which signal a question-and-answer relationship between two parts of the paragraph.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Resentment
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Anger.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Resentment" means a feeling of bitter indignation or anger at having been treated unfairly. (नाराज़गी/रोष)
◦ Example: She felt deep resentment towards her colleague for taking credit for her work.

• "Anger" is the closest synonym, as both words describe a strong feeling of displeasure or hostility.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Calmness" means a state of being free from agitation or excitement — it is nearly opposite to "resentment", not a synonym.

• Option 2: "Happiness" means a state of contentment or joy, which is unrelated to and opposite in feeling to "resentment".

• Option 4: "Relaxation" means freedom from tension or stress, which has no meaningful connection to the bitterness implied by "resentment".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "resentment" useful for SSC: indignation, bitterness, displeasure, rancour, animosity.

• Its antonym is "contentment" or "satisfaction", sometimes tested in antonym-based questions.

question:
Select the option with the correct spelling that can replace the underlined word in the given sentence.
Kasturi acts as a liason between patients and staff.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. liaison.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "liaison" — a person who acts as a link to assist communication or cooperation between groups or organisations; also, the communication link itself.

• Spelling key: LI + AI + SON. Note the "ai" combination in the middle syllable, and the ending "-son" (not "-san" or "-sion"). The word is borrowed from French, from lier, meaning "to bind/link".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "liaision" is incorrect; it wrongly inserts an extra "i" before "son", giving "-ision" instead of "-ison".

• Option 2: "laision" is incorrect; the first syllable is wrongly spelt "la" instead of "liai".

• Option 4: "liaisan" is incorrect; the ending is wrongly spelt "-san" instead of the correct "-son".

NOTE

• Other French-origin words with tricky spellings frequently tested by SSC: bureau, rendezvous, connoisseur, entrepreneur, restaurant, questionnaire, silhouette.

• A useful memory trick: "liaison" contains the small word "ais" in its middle — Liai-son.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Meagre
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Generous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Meagre" means scanty, insufficient, or lacking in quantity or richness. (अल्प/तुच्छ)
◦ Example: The refugees survived on a meagre supply of food and water.

• "Generous" — meaning abundant, ample, or plentiful — is the most appropriate antonym among the given options, being the opposite of "scanty/insufficient".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Regional" means relating to a particular region or area — it has no meaningful opposite relationship with "meagre".

• Option 2: "Racial" means relating to race or ethnicity — it is unrelated in meaning to "meagre".

• Option 3: "Stupid" means lacking intelligence — this is unrelated to the idea of quantity/sufficiency conveyed by "meagre".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "meagre": scanty, sparse, paltry, insufficient, scarce.

• Other antonyms of "meagre": abundant, plentiful, ample, copious, bountiful.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the following sentence.
The politician's pompous rhetoric during the campaign failed to garner much support from the public.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Supercilious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Pompous" means self-important, arrogant, or given to excessive display of dignity or importance. (दिखावटी/घमंडी)
◦ Example: His pompous manner of addressing juniors made him unpopular in the office.

• "Supercilious" means having or showing haughty disdain or contempt for others, which closely matches the arrogant self-importance conveyed by "pompous".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Conciliatory" means intended to placate or pacify — this is nearly opposite to the arrogance implied by "pompous".

• Option 2: "Benign" means gentle, kindly, or harmless — this contradicts the negative, self-important tone of "pompous".

• Option 4: "Diplomatic" means tactful and skilled in dealing with people sensitively — this is the opposite of the tactless self-importance implied by "pompous".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "pompous": arrogant, haughty, pretentious, self-important, vain.

• Its antonyms: modest, humble, unassuming, unpretentious.

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
A. In accordance with hierarchical status
B. Of the services rendered
C. Rewards are given
D. And are not related to the economic value
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. C, A, D, B.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part C ("Rewards are given") is the only part that forms a complete independent clause with a subject and verb, so it must open the sentence.

• Part A ("In accordance with hierarchical status") logically follows C, explaining the basis on which rewards are given.

• Part D ("and are not related to the economic value") continues as a second, connected clause joined by "and", contrasting with A.

• Part B ("of the services rendered") completes the phrase begun in D, specifying what the "economic value" refers to.

• Combining C-A-D-B gives: "Rewards are given in accordance with hierarchical status and are not related to the economic value of the services rendered." — a complete, meaningful sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (A, B, D, C) is incorrect because it begins with a prepositional phrase (A) with no preceding main clause for it to modify, leaving the sentence without a clear subject-verb opening.

• Option 2 (A, D, B, C) is incorrect for the same reason — it opens with A instead of the essential main clause C, and also breaks the D-B phrase relationship ("economic value of the services rendered").

• Option 4 (C, B, A, D) is incorrect because it places B ("of the services rendered") directly after C, which is meaningless without D's "economic value" to attach to.

NOTE

• In jumbled-sentence questions, always look for the part containing the main subject and finite verb (here, "Rewards are given") — it is almost always the anchor/opening part of the sentence.

• Watch for words like "and" joining two parallel ideas (here, "hierarchical status" and "economic value") — the parts on either side of "and" must be logically parallel.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in positive degree of comparison.
She is the dullest child in the class.
option_1: She is very duller in the class.
option_2: Dullest child in the class is she.
option_3: No other child in the class is as dull as she.
option_4: In the class of all she is dull.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. No other child in the class is as dull as she.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "She is the dullest child in the class" is in the Superlative Degree, using "dullest" (the -est form) to show the highest degree of a quality among more than two persons/things.

• Rule — converting Superlative to Positive Degree:
◦ Superlative: Subject + is/are + the + adjective(-est) + noun
◦ Positive: No other + noun + is + as + adjective (positive form) + as + Subject

• Applying the rule: "dullest" is converted to its positive form "dull", and the sentence is restructured as "No other child in the class is as dull as she.", which retains the exact original meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "She is very duller in the class" is grammatically wrong — "duller" is the comparative form and cannot be combined with "very", which is used only with the positive degree.

• Option 2: "Dullest child in the class is she" merely reorders the words of the original superlative sentence; it is still in the superlative degree, not the positive degree, and is also awkwardly constructed.

• Option 4: "In the class of all she is dull" is grammatically incorrect and awkwardly phrased ("class of all" is not standard usage), and does not correctly convey the superlative meaning in positive degree form.

NOTE

• Standard formula for Superlative → Positive: "No other + noun (singular) + is/was + as/so + adjective + as + Subject."

• Similarly, Positive → Superlative: "No other + noun + is + as + adjective + as + Subject" becomes "Subject + is + the + adjective(-est) + noun."

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
Wealthier countries are obligated to fulfil a commitment made in the Paris Agreement to provide $100 billion a year in international climate finance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. breach.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Commitment" means a firm promise or pledge to do something, or the state of being dedicated to fulfilling an obligation. (प्रतिबद्धता/वचनबद्धता)

• "Breach" means the breaking of, or failure to observe, a promise, law, or agreement, which is the direct opposite of honouring a "commitment". (उल्लंघन)

• In the given sentence, "fulfil a commitment" means to honour a pledge; the opposite idea is expressed by "breach" — to violate or fail to honour it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "feeble" means weak or lacking strength — it is unrelated in meaning to "commitment" and is not its antonym.

• Option 2: "drape" means to cover or hang cloth loosely — it has no meaningful relationship with "commitment".

• Option 4: "hale" means strong and healthy (as in "hale and hearty") — it is unrelated to the idea of a promise or pledge.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "commitment": pledge, promise, obligation, vow, undertaking.

• Other antonyms of "commitment": breach, violation, negligence, indifference, unconcern.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment in the following sentence.
Brave people never hide at the moment of decision.
option_4: Turn back the hands of time
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. When the crunch comes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "when the crunch comes" (also "when it comes to the crunch") means at the critical or decisive moment, when a difficult decision or action must actually be taken. (निर्णय की घड़ी में)
◦ Example: He talks confidently about taking risks, but when the crunch comes, he always backs out.

• In the given sentence, "Brave people never hide at the moment of decision" means brave people never hide when the crunch comes — i.e., at the critical, decisive moment.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Beat the clock" (समय से पहले काम पूरा करना): means to finish something before a deadline or time limit — it is about speed, not about a decisive moment.

• Option 3: "A hell of time" (बहुत कठिन समय): means a very difficult or troublesome time/experience — it describes hardship, not a decisive moment of choice.

• Option 4: "Turn back the hands of time" (समय को पीछे मोड़ना): means to return to or relive the past — it has no connection with facing a critical decision.

NOTE

• Other idioms of "critical moment" tested by SSC: "the moment of truth" (the time when a person is tested or a decision must be faced) and "in the nick of time" (at the last possible moment).

• Do not confuse "crunch" (a critical situation) with its literal meaning (a crunching sound), which is unrelated here.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
French is taught to us by Miss Glenn.
option_4: Miss Glenn is teaching us French.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Miss Glenn teaches us French.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "French is taught to us by Miss Glenn" is in the Passive Voice, Simple Present Tense (is/am/are + V3).

• Rule — Simple Present Tense:
◦ Passive: Object + is/am/are + V3 + by + Subject
◦ Active: Subject + V1/V5 + Object

• Applying the rule: the agent "Miss Glenn" (introduced by "by") becomes the subject; since "Miss Glenn" is third person singular, the verb "teach" takes the -es ending (V5) to become "teaches"; and "us", the indirect object, is retained, followed by "French".
◦ Active: Miss Glenn teaches us French.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Miss Glenn taught us French" is incorrect because "taught" is the Simple Past Tense form, whereas the given sentence is in the Simple Present Tense.

• Option 2: "Miss Glenn teach us French" is incorrect because the base form "teach" is not used with the third-person singular subject "Miss Glenn" — it must take the -es ending, i.e., "teaches".

• Option 4: "Miss Glenn is teaching us French" is incorrect because "is teaching" is the Present Continuous Tense, not the Simple Present Tense used in the given passive sentence.

NOTE

• With a third-person singular subject (he/she/it/a proper noun), the Simple Present Tense verb takes an -s/-es ending in the active voice.

• Always match the tense of the active sentence exactly to the tense of the original passive sentence — a common trap is to shift tense unintentionally (as in Options 1 and 4).

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.
Adyasha would have been looked gorgeous in ethnic apparel.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. would have looked.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "look" in the sense of "to appear/seem" (e.g., "look gorgeous", "look beautiful") is an intransitive linking verb — it does not take an object and therefore cannot be used in the passive voice.

• Since "would have been looked" is a passive construction (auxiliary "been" + past participle "looked"), it is grammatically wrong here; the sentence needs the active modal perfect form "would have looked" to correctly mean "would have appeared/seemed".

• Corrected sentence: "Adyasha would have looked gorgeous in ethnic apparel."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "was looked" is incorrect; besides being an impossible passive of an intransitive verb, it also breaks the modal "would have" construction implied by the sentence.

• Option 3: "had looking" is incorrect; this is not a valid verb structure in English — "had" must be followed by a past participle (V3), not the "-ing" form.

• Option 4: "would be looked" is incorrect; it is still a passive construction of the intransitive verb "look" and also changes the intended time reference from a hypothetical past ("would have") to present/future ("would be").

NOTE

• Other common linking/intransitive verbs that cannot be used in the passive voice: appear, seem, become, remain, occur, happen, arise, exist.

• Modal perfect structure for an unfulfilled past possibility: Subject + would/could/should + have + V3 (e.g., "would have looked", "could have won").

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
Babbal is / a oldest member / in our / Black Ice Club.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. a oldest member.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The segment "a oldest member" contains an article error. The indefinite article "a" is used before words beginning with a consonant sound, but superlative adjectives (like "oldest") must always be preceded by the definite article "the", not "a"/"an".

• Corrected segment: "the oldest member".

• Rule: Superlative degree adjectives (words ending in -est, or preceded by "most") always take the definite article "the" — e.g., "the tallest", "the best", "the most beautiful".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "in our" is grammatically correct as used, with no article or agreement error.

• Option 2: "Black Ice Club" is a proper noun (name of the club) and is correctly used without any article requirement.

• Option 3: "Babbal is" is grammatically correct — a proper noun subject correctly followed by the singular verb "is".

NOTE

• Superlative adjectives always require the definite article "the" (e.g., "the fastest runner", "the most intelligent student"), never the indefinite article "a"/"an".

• Common SSC trap: confusing the article rule for superlatives (always "the") with that for ordinary countable nouns (which may take "a"/"an").

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order, except the first part. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
Such poststructuralist pronouncements…
A. not only in the Anglo-American academia
B. on the literature of the Third World,
C. however, are a common feature of the literary theory practiced
D. but also in the Third-World countries
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. BCAD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence begins with the fixed opening "Such poststructuralist pronouncements…", which needs an immediate qualifier telling us what the pronouncements are about.

• Part B ("on the literature of the Third World,") logically completes the opening phrase, specifying the subject of the pronouncements.

• Part C ("however, are a common feature of the literary theory practiced") follows next, introducing the main verb phrase of the sentence with the contrasting connector "however".

• Parts A ("not only in the Anglo-American academia") and D ("but also in the Third-World countries") must appear together in that order, since they form the fixed correlative pair "not only … but also …".

• Combining in the order B-C-A-D gives: "Such poststructuralist pronouncements on the literature of the Third World, however, are a common feature of the literary theory practiced not only in the Anglo-American academia but also in the Third-World countries." — a complete, coherent sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (ABCD) is incorrect because it places the "not only" clause (A) directly after the opening phrase, before the main verb phrase (C) has even been introduced, breaking the sentence's logic.

• Option 2 (ADCB) is incorrect because it separates the correlative pair "not only (A) … but also (D)" from the main clause (C) and misplaces B, destroying the sentence's coherence.

• Option 4 (CABD) is incorrect because it opens with C, leaving the initial phrase "Such poststructuralist pronouncements" without B's necessary qualifier ("on the literature of the Third World") directly attached to it.

NOTE

• The correlative conjunction pair "not only … but also …" must always keep its two parts in that fixed order and joined to grammatically parallel elements.

• When rearranging sentences with a fixed opening phrase, always check which part most directly and grammatically completes that opening phrase — it should follow immediately.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Fundamental
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Least.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Fundamental" means forming a necessary base or core; of central or primary importance. (मौलिक/बुनियादी)
◦ Example: Reading is a fundamental skill needed for all other subjects.

• Among the given options, "Least" — meaning smallest in degree, extent, or importance — is the option that best contrasts with the sense of primary/central importance carried by "fundamental", since something "fundamental" is of the greatest, not the least, importance.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Impact" means a marked effect or influence — it is not opposite in meaning to "fundamental"; it is simply unrelated.

• Option 2: "Neutral" means not aligned with or supporting any side — this describes an absence of position, not a degree of importance, so it is not a true antonym of "fundamental".

• Option 4: "Link" means a connection between two things — it bears no opposite relationship to "fundamental".

NOTE

• More standard antonyms of "fundamental" include: secondary, minor, superficial, unimportant, incidental, trivial.

• More standard synonyms of "fundamental" include: basic, essential, primary, elementary, cardinal, core.

question:
Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank.
Even animals find it difficult to ______ the loss of their loved ones.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. bear.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "bear" means to endure or tolerate (something difficult or painful), which is the meaning required by the sentence: animals find it difficult to endure the loss of their loved ones.

• "Bear" and "bare" are homophones (words that sound alike but have different meanings and spellings): "bear" = to endure/tolerate (or the animal), while "bare" = uncovered/empty.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "wear" means to have clothing or an accessory on one's body — it does not fit the meaning of enduring a loss.

• Option 3: "where" is a question word/relative adverb referring to place or location — it is grammatically impossible in this blank, which requires a verb.

• Option 4: "bare" means uncovered, empty, or without decoration — it does not carry the meaning of "to endure", which the sentence requires.

NOTE

• Commonly confused homophone pairs tested by SSC: bear/bare, where/wear/were, there/their/they're, to/too/two, its/it's.

• Remember: "bear" as a verb (to endure) is different from "bear" as a noun (the animal) — context determines the meaning, but both are spelt the same.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Unemployment arises from a variety of __________(1). One which is always recurring and the effects of which we have had a recent example, is the disorganisation of industry resulting from a long war; this is a serious __________ (2) admitting of no easy__________ (3) at the best of times. Again there is the unemployment which followed a marked diminution in the __________ (4) of any raw product, such as cotton; fewer hands are required in the mills and the factories. We may call this cause of bad harvests. Similar, but more serious is the effect of changes in industry due to the invention of machinery which does more work and require __________ (5) hands. Yet another cause is strike or lockout and this is more to be deplored because such a stoppage is due to a very trivial matter, perhaps the men are working half an hour longer than what their Union permits.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. causes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a plural noun meaning "reasons/origins", since the sentence states unemployment "arises from a variety of ___(1)___", and the rest of the passage goes on to describe several distinct causes of unemployment (war, bad harvests, invention of machinery, strikes/lockouts).

• "Causes" fits both grammatically (plural noun after "a variety of") and contextually, as it correctly previews the list of reasons for unemployment discussed in the rest of the passage.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "thoughts" means ideas or considerations in the mind — it does not fit the context of reasons/origins of unemployment.

• Option 3: "things" is too vague and generic; it does not specifically convey the sense of "reasons" required by the passage's structure.

• Option 4: "types" would suggest kinds/categories of unemployment itself, not reasons for it, which does not match the passage's subsequent description of causes.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always read ahead to the following sentences before choosing a blank's answer — here, the rest of the paragraph (war, harvests, machinery, strikes) confirms that "causes" is the intended sense.

• Common SSC cloze strategy: identify whether the blank needs a cause, effect, example, or contrast, based on the sentences immediately before and after it.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. problem.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a noun that can be described as "serious" and that "admits of no easy" resolution — i.e., something difficult to deal with. "Problem" fits perfectly: "a serious problem admitting of no easy solution."

• The disorganisation of industry resulting from a long war is being described as a difficult issue without a simple fix, which is exactly the sense of "problem".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "difference" means a way in which people/things are unlike — it does not fit the sense of something requiring a solution.

• Option 2: "discussion" means a conversation or debate about a topic — the sentence is not about talking over the issue but about the issue itself being unresolved.

• Option 3: "nature" means the basic character of something — it does not fit grammatically or logically as something that "admits of no easy" resolution.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, match the noun in the blank to the descriptive words around it — here, "serious" and "admitting of no easy [solution]" both point to a difficult "problem".

• Related collocations often tested: "a serious problem", "a knotty problem", "a problem admits of a solution".

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. solution.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase **"admitting of no easy __________" requires a noun that pairs naturally with "problem" from the previous blank — a "problem" is said to "admit of" (allow/have) a "solution"**.

• The complete idea is: "this is a serious problem admitting of no easy solution" — meaning the problem is not easily solved.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "key" can figuratively mean a solution, but it does not fit the standard collocation "admit of a solution/answer" as naturally or correctly here as "solution" does, and is not the best fit in this formal passage.

• Option 2: "clue" means a piece of evidence helping to solve a mystery — it does not fit the collocation "admitting of no easy clue", which is not idiomatic.

• Option 3: "answer" is close in meaning but does not collocate as naturally with "admits of" as "solution" does — a "problem" standardly "admits of a solution", not "an answer" in this formal register.

NOTE

• Common collocation: "a problem admits of a solution" — meaning the problem allows for/has a solution.

• Words like "solution", "resolution" and "remedy" are typically used with "problem", while "answer" is typically used with "question".

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. quantity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes **"a marked diminution [decrease] in the __________ of any raw product, such as cotton", followed by the explanation that "fewer hands are required in the mills and the factories"**.

• Since fewer workers are needed because there is less raw material (cotton) available to process, the blank must refer to the amount/quantity of the raw product, not its quality or material type.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "material" is redundant here, since "raw product" (i.e., raw material) has already been named in the same sentence; it does not fit grammatically with "diminution in the material of any raw product".

• Option 2: "quality" refers to the standard or grade of the product, not the amount produced — a fall in quality would not directly explain why fewer hands are needed in mills and factories.

• Option 4: "cloth" is too specific and incorrect, since the sentence is about raw cotton (a raw material), not the finished cloth product.

NOTE

• Watch for cause-effect logic in cloze passages: here, a decrease in quantity of raw cotton directly causes a decrease in the number of workers needed, which is confirmed by the following clause.

• Common collocation: "a diminution/decrease/reduction in the quantity of" something.

Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Unemployment arises from a variety of __________(1). One which is always recurring and the effects of which we have had a recent example, is the disorganisation of industry resulting from a long war; this is a serious __________ (2) admitting of no easy__________ (3) at the best of times. Again there is the unemployment which followed a marked diminution in the __________ (4) of any raw product, such as cotton; fewer hands are required in the mills and the factories. We may call this cause of bad harvests. Similar, but more serious is the effect of changes in industry due to the invention of machinery which does more work and require __________ (5) hands. Yet another cause is strike or lockout and this is more to be deplored because such a stoppage is due to a very trivial matter, perhaps the men are working half an hour longer than what their Union permits.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. fewer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The noun "hands" (meaning workers/labourers) is a countable plural noun; grammar requires the quantifier "fewer" (not "less") to be used with countable plural nouns.

• Since machinery "does more work", logically it would require a smaller number of workers, so the sense of reduction (fewer hands) fits the context, along with correct grammar.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "more" contradicts the passage's logic — since machinery does more work by itself, it would require fewer, not more, workers.

• Option 3: "many" does not convey the necessary sense of reduction implied by machines doing more work in place of human labour.

• Option 4: "a lot of" similarly fails to convey the reduction in workers required, and does not fit the intended meaning of the sentence as well as "fewer" does.

NOTE

• Rule: "fewer" is used with countable plural nouns (e.g., fewer hands, fewer people, fewer books), while "less" is used with uncountable nouns (e.g., less work, less time, less money).

• This is one of the most frequently tested grammar points in SSC cloze and error-spotting questions — always check whether the noun after "fewer/less" is countable or uncountable.
